notes: Lakes v. warehouses, analytics v. AI/ML, SQL v. everything else... As the technical capabilities of data lakes and data warehouses converge, are the separate tools and teams that run AI/ML and analytics converging as well? In this podcast, originally recorded as part of Fivetran's Modern Data Stack conference, five leaders in data infrastructure debate that question: a16z general partner and pioneer of software defined networking Martin Casado, former CEO of Snowflake Bob Muglia; Michelle Ufford, founder and CEO of Noteable; Tristan Handy, founder of Fishtown Analytics and leader of the open source project dbt; and Fivetran founder George Fraser. The conversation covers the future of data lakes, the new use cases for the modern data stack, data mesh and whether decentralization of teams and tools is the future, and how low we actually need to go with latency. And while the topic of debate is the modern data stack, the themes and differing perspectives strike at the heart of an even bigger: how does technology evolve in complex enterprise environments? thesis: The podcast discusses the debate between data lakes and data warehouses, with Martine Casato arguing that data lakes will eventually consume everything due to their optimization for operational AI and unstructured data, while Bob Muglia contends that SQL-based data warehouses will subsume structured and semi-structured data storage and query capabilities within two to three years. Tristan Handy suggests that while SQL will dominate data processing, data lakes remain necessary today for handling complex data like images and videos that current warehouses cannot process, though he notes that format interoperability issues are diminishing.
